kevin: quick q — setting up API key env + auth headers for SDKs. Python vs Node differences? streaming retries? I keep hitting 401 when testing. TL;DR steps?
maria: which endpoint / deployment (hosted vs dedicated/private)?
kevin: hosted for now. using node fetch. I export REDWOOD_API_KEY and do fetch with Authorization: Bearer, still 401.
sophia: common gotchas: env var not loaded (dotenv), wrong var name (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY), trailing newline in files, shell didn't export. also check account/workspace key. can you paste snippet?
kevin: here's the minimal snippet i'm running:
```js
// index.js
const res = await fetch("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: "hi" })
});
```
maria: looks sane. common node stuff: if you're using dotenv, require it before reading env. if using nodemon make sure it reloads env. for mac/linux do `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...` in same shell. also verify no stray quotes/newlines.
ian: also check whether your workspace is on hosted or dedicated/private — some private setups require Basic auth (api-key as username or as password). curl -u can sometimes succeed where Bearer fails.
kevin: interesting — i tried `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY'` and got 401, but `curl -u "$REDWOOD_API_KEY:"` worked. what's the canonical thing?
sophia: if your instance expects Basic auth then use Basic. two quick examples:
```bash
# curl using curl -u (sends Basic):
curl -u "$REDWOOD_API_KEY:" "https://private.redwood.local/v1/chat"

# explicit header (base64 of api_key:):
AUTH=$(echo -n "$REDWOOD_API_KEY:" | base64)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $AUTH" https://private.redwood.local/v1/chat
```
maria: for Node header example: `Authorization: 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY + ':').toString('base64')`
kevin: ahhh that explains it, thanks. streaming: i'm using fetch streaming and i get chunked text but the SDK has helpers that return events. any known quirks?
devex-bot: FYI — Redwood JS SDK streaming returns an AsyncIterable of events; plain fetch yields a ReadableStream. see /sdk/streaming in docs.
sophia: yep. plain fetch is lower-level — use `response.body.getReader()` + TextDecoder or use the SDK's parser. axios needs `responseType: 'stream'` and then pipe/parse. note: some proxies will buffer chunking which can make streaming appear delayed.
ian: retries: transient 429/5xx are common. our generic HTTP client will retry idempotent requests by default (GETs). for POST streaming endpoints we don't auto-retry because replaying partial streams is unsafe. implement resumable logic or use server-side cursors if available.
kevin: where to configure retry counts/backoff in SDK?
maria: client opts example (pseudo): `{ retries: 3, backoff: { baseMs: 200, maxMs: 5000 }, retryOn: [429, 503] }`. exact keys depend on lang SDK but same idea.
kevin: last quick one — windows: setx vs $env:, what's recommended for dev?
sophia: PowerShell quick: temporary for session: `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk_...'`. to persist: `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY 'sk_...'` then reopen shell. cmd.exe: `set REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...` for session.
kevin: awesome, i'll update our README with two snippets (curl + node + python). thanks all! :rocket:
maria: thanks — paste your final snippet and i'll add it to the devex quickstart and the SDK FAQ.
kevin: will do in a few mins — ping me if i forget :slightly_smiling_face:
